Corporate Car Service in Scottsdale and Phoenix

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a corporate car service across Scottsdale and Phoenix: a professional chauffeur, a vehicle reserved for your company's people, and a price fixed from the published rate card before anyone travels. Book it as a one-way trip or by the hour. Rates run $125 to $295 an hour on a 4-hour minimum, so a corporate car starts at $500 before 8% Arizona sales tax in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), and a one-way trip starts at $225.

Last updated: September 28, 2026

What is a corporate car service, and is it the same as an executive car service?

A corporate car service is a chauffeured vehicle that a company books for its own people or its guests: an executive landing at the airport, a client between meetings, a leadership team on a day with several stops. Executive car service means the same thing here. There is one rate card, one set of vehicles and one way to book, whichever phrase you searched. The person booking may not be the person riding. An assistant, a travel desk or an event planner books, and the chauffeur works from what the booking says on the day, so the useful part of the service is the written detail: the vehicle, the addresses, the times and the price, all confirmed before the trip. Two lines from the inclusion list printed on the corporate transportation page carry the trust part: "A professional chauffeur on every vehicle, background- and MVR-checked" and "A permitted, licensed and insured, locally owned operator".

What does a corporate car service cost in Scottsdale and Phoenix?

By the hour or by the trip. The car-class vehicles run $125 to $295 an hour, each on a 4-hour minimum, so the starting total is the rate times 4 hours before tax: $500 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), $580 in either Executive Sprinter and $1,180 in the Maybach Jet Sprinter. A trip is one move between two addresses at a published price, with no hours to count: $225 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), $295 in an Executive Sprinter and $550 in the Maybach Jet Sprinter. A trip is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off; a longer one is priced from the drive, with the empty return included. You reserve the vehicle, not seats, so a full cabin lowers the cost per rider. Split evenly across every seat at the minimum, the Executive Black Sprinter comes to about $41 a head, a planning figure only. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout. A long day gets cheaper by the hour: "Free hours as the day gets longer: 7–11 hours earns 1, 12–14 earns 2, 15 or more earns 3". An 8-hour day in the Executive Black Sprinter therefore bills 7 hours, $1,015 before tax.

Which vehicle should the company book for an executive, a client or a team?

Take the smallest vehicle that clears the headcount and the bags, then step up for the passenger rather than the price. The car class seats 6 to 14, and every unit in it is chauffeured. One or two travelers with bags: the Luxury SUV (Suburban) seats 6 at $125 an hour, with room for 10 bags. It carries the lowest hourly rate in the car class. It suits an airport arrival or a single meeting. Leadership between meetings: the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter seats 8 in Maybach seats that recline, ventilate and massage, at $195 an hour. It takes no luggage, so it is for the ride, not the airport haul. The Maybach Jet Sprinter seats 9 at $295 an hour and takes 4 checked bags and 8 carry-ons: a private-jet cabin for a small executive group. A team or a client party up to 14: an Executive Sprinter, black or white, at $145 an hour. Both have room for 40 bags, loaded into the rear compartment, so a full cabin and a full load of bags travel together. The white one is the black in white, with the same leather seats. Above 14 riders the movement is a shuttle rather than a car. The executive coaches seat 24 to 56 and are priced on the executive minibus and group shuttle page. Size also changes the terms: "Groups of 20+ passengers, or any booking with two or more vehicles, carry the large-group cancellation window rather than the standard one."

Should a corporate day be booked by the trip or by the hour?

Book the trip for one movement with no waiting, and the hour once the vehicle has to stay with you. The line between them is arithmetic on the rate card. Take the Executive Black Sprinter. One trip is $295. Booked together with the way back, the return earns the 20% return credit and costs $236, so there and back is $531, less than the $580 minimum block. Two separate one-way trips come to $590, already more than the block. Add a third movement and the comparison turns: three legs come to $826, more than the block. A day of arrival, meeting, lunch and dinner is a block; a lone arrival is a trip. Stops matter too. Each added stop on a trip is $50, outbound and return alike, while stops inside an hourly block cost nothing, and a longer wait is simply more hours at the same rate. Keep the trip for a straight run and the hour for a day that loops.

How does a corporate car service handle airport pickups for a visiting executive?

As a trip or inside an hourly block, with the flight tracked. Scottsdale Sprinters holds the Phoenix Sky Harbor (PHX) ground transportation permit. Put the airline and flight number on the reservation. Your traveler stays in baggage claim until the chauffeur sends the pickup instruction for their terminal; this page names no curb, door or terminal, and the Phoenix airport guide carries that detail. A greeter who meets the traveler at baggage claim with a name sign and helps with the bags is an optional $200 add-on on an airport transfer. The Scottsdale page names Phoenix Sky Harbor International (PHX) and Scottsdale Airport (SCF), and Phoenix-Mesa Gateway has its own group transportation page for the east-side arrival. A guest flying in alone suits the Luxury SUV (Suburban), with room for 10 bags. Several guests on one flight take an Executive Sprinter, and separate flights can be separate trips or one hourly block that waits.

Can one booking move a whole team or several vehicles?

Yes. One reservation takes up to 3 of the same unit where we run more than one. Up to 42 across 3 Executive Black Sprinters. The units a booking can multiply are the Executive Black Sprinters and Executive White Sprinters. The Luxury SUV (Suburban), Maybach Shuttle Sprinter and Maybach Jet Sprinter are single units, so a booking cannot multiply them; a party that outgrows one adds a different vehicle on request. A bigger movement is a coordinated program. The desk arranges on request: "Several vehicles on one booking, coordinated to one schedule with one point of contact" and "A written movement plan before the date — vehicle by vehicle, pickup by pickup".

What is included in a corporate car service booking, and what costs extra?

In the price: the chauffeur, the vehicle for the booked time and bottled water. The last line of the inclusion list covers the fees: "Tax only — no booking fee, no service charge, no fuel surcharge, and gratuity never added for you". Everything beyond the water is an add-on you choose at checkout. Bottled water is on board for every ride and it is the only complimentary amenity; a greeter, refreshments, a custom sign or a child seat are add-ons you choose at checkout. The corporate menu prices a snack pack at $150 and refreshments at $150 on a trip or an hourly booking, and a branded welcome sign at $95 on an hourly booking. The airport greeter is $200.

What does an assistant or travel desk need to have ready to book?

Six things: the date and pickup time, the street address of every pickup and drop-off, the number of passengers, the bag count, the mobile number of whoever will meet the vehicle, and for an arrival the airline and flight number. Two of those decide the day, and the desk states them this way: "Put a street address on the reservation rather than a landmark, and give us the mobile number of whoever is actually meeting the vehicle." For a team carrying more than suitcases, list banner cases, pop-up displays, sample boxes and crew gear when you request the quote, so the fit is confirmed in writing before the vehicle is chosen.

Where does a corporate car service pick up across Scottsdale and Phoenix?

Across every city with a published service-area page: Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. The published hourly rate is the same in each, so a Tempe pickup is booked exactly like a Scottsdale one. Inside Scottsdale the published areas run from Old Town Scottsdale to North Scottsdale. On an hourly booking the drive between your stops is part of the hours you reserved; on a trip the price covers the route you gave.

How do the quote, payment and cancellation work for a company booking?

The price is on the page for a standard booking, and anything the online quote cannot price comes back in writing first. Give us a headcount and a schedule and we will tell you how many vehicles it takes, in writing, before anything is charged. How the rest settles depends on how you pay: on a card, a 50% deposit holds the date and your written confirmation sets out the balance and its timing; paying in full at checkout leaves nothing else due before your ride; a payment link from the reservations desk opens that same checkout. Free cancellation applies up to 14 days before pickup on a standard booking; major-event dates and large groups carry their own windows, published in full on the policies page. Questions before you book go to (623) 986-6339 by call or text, or to reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com. Rides run around the clock; quotes are answered 8am–8pm Arizona time, seven days.
